stem: Two candles, A and B, are lit at the same time, and each burns at its own constant rate. Candle A is 30 centimeters tall when it is lit, and its height decreases by 2 centimeters per hour. Five hours after they are lit, the two candles have the same height. Candle B burns out completely 2 hours before candle A does. What was the height, in centimeters, of candle B when it was lit?
solution: Candle A: \(A(t) = 30 - 2t\). It burns out when \(t = 15\), and \(A(5) = 20\).
Candle B is also 20 centimeters tall at \(t = 5\) and burns out at \(t = 13\), so it loses 20 centimeters in 8 hours: 2.5 centimeters per hour.
verify:
t, h0, r = symbols('t h0 r')
A = 30 - 2*t
tA = solve(A, t)[0]
B = h0 - r*t
sol = solve([Eq(B.subs(t, 5), A.subs(t, 5)), Eq(B.subs(t, tA - 2), 0)], [h0, r], dict=True)
assert sol == [{h0: Rational(65, 2), r: Rational(5, 2)}]
assert [Rational(s) for s in spr_answers] == [Rational(65, 2)]
